items.title: Press Briefing Note by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: The Government of Nepal is conducting search, rescue, relief and recovery operations across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan districts following the Bhote Koshi River floods of 26 August 2026, with priority given to locating missing persons including both Nepali and foreign nationals. So far 626 bodies have been recovered, over 4450 people have been rescued including over 187 foreign nationals, and about 2400 people remain unaccounted for. A dedicated Emergency Control Room at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is coordinating with families, local administrations and diplomatic missions to share verified information and facilitate assistance.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing Note by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 28 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods struck the Bhote Koshi River area on 26 August 2026, causing loss of life, displacement, and damage to infrastructure. As of 15:30 NST on 28 August 2026, 538 bodies have been recovered, while 121 out of 632 people from 33 countries have been found and 511 remain missing. Security and disaster-management agencies continue search, rescue, and relief operations.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 28 August 2026

items.title: FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang
items.summary: Rescue operations intensified Thursday at the mudslide-stricken Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border, with 141 rescuers arriving that morning along with helicopters for assessment and search missions. As of 8 a.m. Thursday, three people had been killed, 558 others remained missing, and two local villagers had been rescued after the mudslide struck Wednesday morning. Additional teams including 111 China Search and Rescue personnel, an advance engineering group, and Red Cross supplies such as tents and emergency kits have been dispatched to the area.
items.citation: Xinhua (Gyirong / Tibet side) — FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang

items.title: NOTICE: Emergency Control Room (ECR) for Assistance regarding Foreign Nationals Affected by the Bhote Koshi Flash Flood
items.summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has established an Emergency Control Room to coordinate search, rescue, information verification, and consular assistance for foreign nationals affected by or missing in the Rasuwa flash flood. Families may contact the ECR via WhatsApp/hotline at +977-9744441227 or +977-9744441228 (7am–10pm) or email for verified information. Official updates are published at https://mofa.gov.np/category/flashflood/.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — NOTICE: Emergency Control Room (ECR) for Assistance regarding Foreign Nationals Affected by the Bhote Koshi Flash Flood

items.title: Special Control Room in MEA for Nepal Floods Situation
items.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs has established a 24×7 Special Control Room in Delhi for the Nepal floods situation. Contact options include the control room numbers +91 11 2308 8718, +91 11 2308 8719, and +91 11 2301 2113, plus WhatsApp +91 9968291988 and email situationroom@mea.gov.in. Indian embassies in Kathmandu and Beijing provide additional WhatsApp contacts, along with Nepali authorities including Tourist Police, Nepal Army, NDRRMA, and district officers for Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, and Chitwan.
items.citation: MEA press release — Special Control Room in MEA for Nepal Floods Situation

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 26 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods struck the Bhote Koshi River area on 26 August 2026, causing loss of life, displacement, and damage to homes, roads, bridges, and hydropower facilities. 72 bodies have been recovered so far, while 403 people from 25 countries (203 males and 200 females, including 62 Nepali nationals) are reported missing. Security agencies and authorities are conducting search and rescue, evacuation, and relief operations.

items.source: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA)
items.title: NDRRMA rescue coordination portal
items.summary: NDRRMA publishes rescue and coordination updates for the Bhotekoshi/Rasuwa flash flood on its official rescue portal and the SETU platform at setu.ndrrma.gov.np. Families should check these official channels for status rather than unofficial social media reposts. The linked site directs to NDRRMA and does not copy individual case data.

items.title: Nepal Police official found and missing lists
items.summary: Nepal Police maintains the official Unified Database for missing persons, found persons, and unidentified remains related to the flood-affected areas. Families can search the database at udb.nepalpolice.gov.np/missing and udb.nepalpolice.gov.np/found. Official confirmation of status comes only from Nepal Police and not from volunteer sites or social media.

items.title: Embassy of India, Kathmandu — assistance for Indian nationals
items.summary: The Embassy of India in Kathmandu is coordinating with Nepalese authorities on search and rescue for Indian nationals affected by flash floods in the Rasuwa/Bhotekoshi area. Indian nationals and families may contact the MEA Special Control Room in Delhi at +91-11-23088718, +91-11-23088719, WhatsApp +91-9968291988, or situationroom@mea.gov.in. The Embassy can also be reached via WhatsApp at +977-9851316807.
